failure_summary.description: Possessive/owner clues ('his 1983 album', 'he worked on his painting', 'this organization's Hall of Fame') were answered with the work, album or sub-part named in the clue instead of the person or organization that owns or made it.
A verbatim archive answer ('Anchorage, Alaska') was shortened to the bare city, so Rule 4 shortening overrode Rule 3's copy-in-full rule.
The fragment '...on my mind' was answered with a singer, the artist of the top hit, instead of the missing word that completes a famous title.
'Highland version of this instrument' was answered with the modifier plus a singular form ('Great Highland Bagpipe') instead of the bare plural family name.

The superlative clue 'cost greater than all other wars put together' was answered with the earlier of two sequel candidates (WWI instead of WWII). The agent did not check which candidate satisfies the comparison.
A bare list of three countries was answered with a category label ('Nordic countries'), but the gold key was one of the listed items. This is ambiguous and not fixable by a general rule.

patch.reasoning: Earlier steps added large mandatory-answer-line blocks and every one was rejected. These edits are small, targeted bullets instead. (1) Three failures were the same slot error: answering the work or part named in a possessive clue instead of its owner or creator. (2) Verbatim archive answers keep being shortened by Rule 4, here and in step 33, so Rule 3 needs an explicit copy-in-full override. (3) The ellipsis-fragment rule exists but is too terse and the agent answered with the artist. (4) The 'version of this' rule needs to cover the modifier-drop plus family-name case, and a comparison/superlative check is missing for sequel-type candidates.

edits.target: - 'One of these <role/title>' ('the 14th one of these spiritual leaders') asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content: - POSSESSIVE / OWNER clues: when the clue names a work, album, song, painting or sub-part and attaches it to 'he / she / his / her / this <org>'s' ('"X" is the last song on his 1983 album "Y"', 'he worked on his "Virgin and Child..."', 'A & B are in this organization's Hall of Fame, founded in 1967'), the answer is the PERSON or ORGANIZATION that made or owns it. Never answer with the work, the album, another work by the same person, or the part named in the clue ('Hall of Fame'). If your candidate is a title or phrase already quoted in the clue, or something the clue's subject made or contains, it is the wrong slot. Also test the clue's identifying detail ('founded in 1967', a year, a number) against the candidate and choose the body that has it, not a larger related body.

edits.target: Before the answer tags, briefly quote the matched line.
edits.content: - COPY IN FULL: Rule 4's shortening rules (drop qualifiers, drop 'a/the', singularize, drop descriptors) do NOT apply to a verbatim archive answer. Keep everything the archive shows: a city's ', State' or ', Country' ('Anchorage, Alaska', not 'Anchorage'), a trailing noun ('a eucalyptus tree', not 'Eucalyptus'), a plural, a leading 'the'. Strip only the contestant text ('. right: Name', 'wrong:') and any 'What is / Who is' wrapper.

edits.target: The context passages about the topic usually reveal the link.
edits.content: - A quoted fragment that starts or ends with '...' (e.g. '"...on my mind"') asks for the MISSING WORD(S) that complete a famous title, phrase or lyric. It does NOT ask for the singer, author, band or work that contains it. Scan the passage titles for other items of the form '<Word> on my mind' and give the word that completes the best-known classic title. Do not stop at the first hit, which is often a recent song by a modern artist. Never answer with a performer's name.

edits.target: Other clue details (diet, ingredient, cooking method) are just conditions on the generic dish.
edits.content:
- The same holds for '<Modifier> version of this <generic noun>' ('the Highland version of this instrument'): the modifier is only a hint and is NOT part of the answer. Answer with the bare family name exactly as the passages title the family, keeping a plural headword plural. Do not output the modifier plus a singular ('Great Highland Bagpipe').
- SUPERLATIVE / COMPARISON clues ('greater than all other X put together', 'the most', 'the largest'): the answer must beat every other candidate, including the earlier or later numbered entity that appears in the passages. When the archive hit is cut off before the answer, decide with your own knowledge which candidate makes the comparison true. A later, larger event or entity that includes the earlier one wins over the earlier one.
